target_customer: Research scientists and teams in biology (starting with protein and sequence analysis) who use computational tools, models and agents
problem: Researchers must assemble data, choose methods and make tools and models work together, often wrestling with Python environments and GPUs; results are hard to trace and share between people and agents.
business_model: Free tier plus paid model runs and individual and team plans for the Noto workbench; data access and private evaluations by inquiry
product_category: Scientific discovery workbench, protein language models and scientific software

founders.name: Casey Mogilevsky
founders.background_notes: YC page: advised by Matt Francis and Jennifer Doudna as an undergraduate, first author JACS paper, co-invented patent underlying Catena Bio (YC S21), began a collaboration with David Baker's lab that became part of Archon Bio. Team size is 1.

competitors.name: EvolutionaryScale
competitors.what: ESM3 protein language model with a Forge developer platform

competitors.name: Profluent Bio
competitors.what: Frontier AI models for programmable biology and protein design

competitors.name: Google Co-Scientist
competitors.what: Multi-agent AI system built on Gemini for generating and debating research hypotheses

technical_complexity.rationale: Pretraining protein language models, differentiable alignment libraries, an inference compiler and a multiplayer workbench for one founder is research-grade work across several fronts.

defensibility.rationale: Large assembled protein sequence and structure collections and learned alignment methods are hard to copy, but funded rivals and open models compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded protein model companies and platforms were already active; Benchling later described a multiplayer agent environment in October 2026.

market_need_then: Rapid growth in protein models and agentic science in 2025 and 2026 and heavy funding of protein AI companies point to demand for tools that combine data, models and agents; the company says free usage is live.

branding.domain_note: Uses orikata.ai for the company and orikata.bio and megure.ai for brands.

identity.logo: Orikata Bio uses a sakura mark; Megure Labs has its own mark
identity.visual_style: Wisteria and sakura illustrations in light and dark versions
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and descriptive, with Japanese inspired product names such as Hikoboshi and Orihime

branding.brand_signature: Japanese inspired naming across products and sakura and wisteria imagery
branding.community_and_virality: Open source projects Hikoboshi and Orihime are on GitHub; no press about the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive visual and naming theme, but two brands under one legal entity and no press or community evidence yet; name is easily confused with Orikine Bio.

outcome_analysis: Orikata Bio PBC is an Active Summer 2026 company with a single founder and no outcome yet. It spreads across models, open source libraries, an inference compiler and a workbench, which shows ambition but risks focus. Funded protein AI companies and platforms such as Benchling, which described a multiplayer agent environment in October 2026, raise the competitive bar. No acquisition or shutdown news was found.
notes: No funding, news or independent coverage found; searches for the company, product names and founder returned unrelated companies such as Orikine Bio. YC lists the name as a PBC; the long description mentions two brands, Orikata Bio and Megure Labs. The YC page lists Casey Mogilevsky as sole founder; the surname is from the YC page.
